info.title: Crossfeed API
info.description: Act for one network: its roster, launches, and inbox. Authenticate with one of the network's API keys, made by an owner in its settings, as `Authorization: Bearer cf_live_…`. Nothing here approves an insertion order or a reply: only a member does, in the app. Long work, such as an import, answers 202 with the resource's current status; poll the resource until it settles. Examples use made-up shows and figures.

additionalProperties.description: Above 0, its listeners lean toward this group, relative to the average in Qloo; below 0, away from it. Qloo sends three decimals.

age.description: Its lean by age band, youngest first, each as Qloo names it: `24_and_younger`, `25_to_29`, `30_to_34`, `35_to_44`, `45_to_54` and `55_and_older`.

male.description: Its lean toward male listeners; below 0, toward female ones. Qloo's lean toward female listeners is always its negative. Crossfeed counts a gender lean only from 0.2 either way.

Lean.description: A show's leans, which describe its listeners, not people.

post.description: Send the roster file as the body: a CSV with a `name` column and optional `downloads`, `status`, and `description` columns, or plain text with one show name per line, at most 50 shows and 5 MB. It answers 202 at once with the new shows pending; poll the roster until it settles. Over a roster that has shows, it needs `replace=true`: shows already on it keep their matches, comps, and exclusions, the figures the file brings change, and only new shows are looked up.

post.description: Ranks the rest of the roster against each show matched in Qloo, one Qloo call each, counting shows on the same Qloo show once and including shows left out of launches. It takes at least 4 such shows and a roster with no lookup pending, and is refused while a measure runs. It answers 202 at once with the overlap measuring; poll it until it isn't. With the roster's matched shows unchanged, it asks only the shows whose ranking is missing or failed, so it's up to one call per show, and none once every ranking has landed. It counts against the network's daily Qloo calls, and is refused when the Qloo requests left today, Crossfeed's shared ones or the network's own key's, couldn't take it and still leave a run's 60.

post.description: Send the pitches as the body: one email as `message/rfc822` (an .eml file), an mbox export as `application/mbox`, plain text with a line of three dashes between pitches as `text/plain` (a pitch's first lines may give its `From:` and `Subject:`), or JSON pitches, at most 50 pitches and 5 MB. Of each email, only its sender, subject, and text are kept, never its attachments or other headers, and only its work's title and type reach Qloo. An email with no text, or over 10,000 characters, is skipped and named. It answers 202 at once with the pitches reading; poll the inbox until it's done. Reading the pitches counts as one of the network's model runs. Over an inbox that has pitches, it needs `replace=true`: they go, with the last pitch run's lists and replies, and a pitch run waiting on a question ends.
